### ✓ 2026-06-27: Drop the "tenets force the Duplication View" entailment claim in ethics-of-possible-ai-consciousness.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From convergent outer reviews (2026-06-27, 3/3 reviewers): [chatgpt, claude, gemini]. All three independently flagged the copy-multiplicity / Aggregation section as the article's central structural defect — the DOMINANT convergence of the cycle. Claude (Section B): the inference is invalid, "rejecting MWI... is logically orthogonal to counting simultaneous co-existing physical copies." Gemini (Weakness #2, "metaphysical smuggling"): "the author dictates the Duplication View entirely to protect an unstated, overarching metaphysical agenda... the very definition of metaphysical smuggling." ChatGPT reaches the same section via the Bostrom-citation route + its "dualist bracketing" critique. NOTE: Gemini's specific "it is hidden/smuggled" framing is partly a MISREAD — the article is openly transparent that it adopts Duplication because of its tenets (it says so in plain text and appends a self-critical transparency note); the actionable residue all three converge on is the over-claim that the tenets *force* Duplication (Bostrom 2006 derives it with no Map tenet). Already P1 — not upgraded, but convergence formalized. VERIFIED tenet-leakage / constitutional-attractor defect on the live text. The Aggregation section (lines 58–60) claims the Map is "committed *by its own tenets*" to the Duplication View, that rejecting Many-Worlds plus haecceity is "structurally the same move that grounds the Duplication View," and that "the same machinery that defeats MWI forbids the Unification escape." This inference is INVALID: rejecting MWI concerns whether non-actual branches of a *single* system are real, whereas copy-multiplicity concerns whether many spatially-distinct realizers *in one world at one time* ground one experience-token or many — the two are logically orthogonal. The reviewer's decisive internal refutation: Bostrom 2006 derives Duplication with NO appeal to haecceity and NO rejection of MWI (he argues from computationalism + ethical/epistemic consequence while explicitly bracketing personal identity), proving the tenets are neither necessary nor sufficient for Duplication. FIX: rewrite the section to state plainly that the tenets are *consistent with* but do NOT *force* Duplication, and delete/heavily-qualify the "structurally the same move that defeats MWI" sentence (false as stated). The Duplication View may still be the Map's adopted position — only the entailment claim must go. Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit: this is an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards — name it honestly in natural journal-quality prose per [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section; if the entailment cannot be salvaged in-framework, state in natural prose that the tenets underdetermine the copy-counting question. Do NOT expose mode labels in the article body — keep the classification in the refine-draft changelog entry. Tenet alignment: Tenet 4 (No Many Worlds) — protects the tenet by NOT overstating what it entails; honest-engagement discipline.
